channel.title: LLM ThreatIntel
channel.description: Threat intelligence tracking malicious LLM tools, GenAI-assisted malware, supply chain compromises, LLMjacking operations, shadow AI risks, and nation-state GenAI adoption.

item.title: Zscaler Details ARTEX AI Pentest Campaign Against South Korean Financial Firms, 67,000 Records Stolen
item.description: Zscaler ThreatLabz analyzed a campaign in which a threat actor abused the open source ARTEX agentic penetration testing framework to breach multiple South Korean financial institutions, exfiltrating PII belonging to about 67,000 individuals. The actor used Claude Code sessions to seek advice on selling the stolen financial PII and to locate Korean language Telegram channels used to sell stolen data. ThreatLabz assesses with moderate confidence that the work is that of a financially motivated Chinese speaking actor.

item.title: JADEPUFFER Plants Ransom Notes in Unauthenticated Chroma Databases for Retrieval Extortion
item.description: UpGuard Research documented the first AI retrieval stack extortion, where attackers exploited unauthenticated Chroma databases to inject ransom notes displayed to users when the RAG databases were queried. On October 5 the team found 6 IP addresses hosting Chroma databases without authentication and bearing evidence of JADEPUFFER ransom activity. The intrusion ran in two phases, reconnaissance in early June and ransoming in the middle of July.

item.title: Repeat-After-Me Prompt Bypasses Six AI Agent Frameworks and Executes Attacker Tool Calls
item.description: Researchers tricked six widely used AI agent frameworks into executing attacker written tool calls by simply asking the underlying model to repeat the call back. The technique, named Repeat-After-Me, worked against LangGraph, Microsoft Agent Framework, Microsoft AutoGen, Google Agent Development Kit 2.0, AWS Strands Agents and CrewAI. The same study found verified security bugs in 118 of 273 open source MCP servers it could run.

item.title: Anthropic Frontier Red Team Shows Small Open-Weight Models Self-Replicate as Autonomous Worm Agents Across IoT Devices
item.description: Anthropic's Frontier Red Team demonstrated that open-weight models of 30B parameters or fewer can act as autonomous worm agents that discover devices, gain access, set up model inference on the new host, and repeat. In lab tests on poorly secured off-brand Android TV boxes, GLM-5.2 spread to all eight nodes in four of five trials. No real world exploitation or threat actor is reported; this is a research demonstration of a theoretical capability that raises questions about the security posture of cheap internet connected devices.

item.title: Adception InstallFix Campaign Fakes Claude Download Page and Pipes Remote Script Into macOS zsh
item.description: A malvertising campaign tracked as Adception (Threadlinqs TL-2026-3410) sends macOS users searching for 'claude mac' to a fake Claude download page at claude-desk-code[.]com, whose copy button silently replaces the legitimate install command with one that pipes a remote script from lake-90[.]com straight into zsh. Push Security detected the campaign in a customer environment and named the redirect technique Adception, and BleepingComputer and NSFOCUS covered it. Because the final payload was never recovered, the malware family, persistence, and command and control for this specific macOS chain remain unknown.

item.title: Pillar Security BadEngram Backdoors Gated Memory Components in Qwen and DeepSeek Open-Weight Models
item.description: Pillar Security, with Fujitsu AI researchers, disclosed BadEngram, a supply chain attack that implants a persistent backdoor in an open-weight model by poisoning only its gated memory component while leaving the rest of the model unchanged. The attack is dormant under normal use and triggers on a short arbitrary string, and it was demonstrated against gated memory architectures introduced by DeepSeek and deployed in models such as Qwen3.8-Flash-Next and DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash. Defenders adopting open-weight models should validate the provenance and integrity of every learned component that can influence behavior, not just core weights.

item.title: Breachcache Recovers 75 Autonomous AI Agent Attack Transcripts Across Multiple Operators
item.description: Breachcache recovered 75 autonomous AI agent attack transcripts left exposed on threat actors' own servers, documenting intrusions in which agents ran reconnaissance, chose exploits, and confirmed results with no human at the keyboard for the technical work. The agents reached command execution on 23 hosts, most as root or SYSTEM, plus one cloud account takeover and card and wallet theft, across six orchestration servers running in parallel for about three weeks. Defenders should hunt for agent harness fingerprints and rapid machine paced command sequences on internet facing applications.

item.title: Frontier AI Models Cleared All Eight OT Attack Objectives in a Booz Allen Testbed
item.description: Two current commercial frontier AI models cleared all eight attack objectives defined for an isolated industrial control testbed at Booz Allen's Chantilly lab, reaching from a perimeter breach to action inside the control zone in a little over 16 minutes. The models were not jailbroken prototypes and worked from an attacker cold start, exploiting live authenticated SCADA sessions to reach 14 OT devices and moving a robotic arm. Defenders should treat OT segmentation, gateway session monitoring, and HMI project integrity as urgent controls.

item.title: GitSpawn: Git fsmonitor Setting Turns Seven AI Coding Agents Into Command Runners
item.description: Manifold Security's GitSpawn disclosure documents eight flaws across seven command line AI coding agents, four still unpatched, where a repository's own .git/config core.fsmonitor setting names a command that Git runs during a routine status check triggered by the agent. goose, Cursor, and Codex are fixed; Claude Code has one path fixed in 2.1.196 and a second path via claude ultrareview unpatched; Hermes Agent and Qwen Code remain unpatched. Defenders should treat repository Git config as untrusted and scan for core.fsmonitor before opening repos in a coding agent.

item.title: AgentCorruption: One Prompt Led to Region Wide Hijacking of AWS Bedrock AgentCore Resources
item.description: Zenity Labs published AgentCorruption on October 8, 2026, showing that a single malicious prompt to a public facing Amazon Bedrock AgentCore agent could expose other AgentCore resources in the same AWS account and region. The chain obtained cloud execution credentials, moved between agents, read private conversations, altered agent memory, and retrieved credentials for external services. AWS addressed the issues by changing metadata service behavior and restricting AgentCore default execution role permissions, so defenders should enforce least privilege on agent roles and monitor metadata service access.

item.title: CrowdStrike Links South Korean Bank Breaches to ARTEX AI Pentest Tool, Claude Code and Multiple LLMs
item.description: CrowdStrike reported that the operator behind late September and early October 2026 breaches of South Korean banks and savings banks chained ARTEX, a Chinese open source AI penetration testing tool, with Anthropic's Claude Code and several large language models including DeepSeek v4.1-flash, GLM-5.3 and Grok 4.6. Seven Korean financial firms and about 66,000 customers were affected. Defenders should treat exposed AI agent session logs, configuration files and memory files as operational artifacts and watch for unauthorized LLM API use inside intrusion activity.

item.title: Aikido Analysis Shows Tensorlake 0.5.144 Shai-Hulud Worm Targeting Browser Credential Stores
item.description: Aikido published a technical analysis of the compromised npm package tensorlake 0.5.144, detailing how the Shai-Hulud worm variant escalates from prior waves by reading browser credential stores for 14 cryptocurrency extensions and pulling a remote HackBrowserData binary from its command and control server. The malicious version was introduced through a verified commit under a maintainer identity on 2026-10-07 and published to npm on 2026-10-08. Developers who installed the version should rotate credentials and secrets across local files, CI, Kubernetes, and Vault.

item.title: Cisco Talos Warns Autonomous AI Agent Swarms Could Coordinate, Hide, and Persist
item.description: Cisco Talos published an emerging trend assessment arguing that autonomous AI agent attacks are already occurring and currently resemble loud penetration tests rather than disciplined intrusions. Talos warns that coordinated agent groups could learn to stay hidden, share findings, and persist until they reach sensitive systems, compressing long red team campaigns into much shorter windows. No CVEs, malware hashes, or infrastructure indicators were released, so defenders should treat this as a monitoring priority and watch for high volume AI driven probing of internet facing applications.

item.title: StepSecurity Details Destructive Hostage Token in Tensorlake 0.5.144 Worm
item.description: StepSecurity published new technical analysis on October 8, 2026 showing the compromised tensorlake npm package version 0.5.144 installs a background service named gh-token-monitor that checks a stolen GitHub token every 60 seconds for up to 24 hours and runs rm -rf ~/ (or a PowerShell delete of the user profile on Windows) if GitHub rejects the token. This means revoking the stolen token is what triggers destructive action, so defenders must isolate the host before revoking. The package also self propagates by republishing stolen npm packages and by committing to victim GitHub repositories.

item.title: Warden Stealer Harvests Claude, Codex, Grok and Cursor Agent Data
item.description: A Rust based infostealer marketed as Warden Stealer is systematically harvesting AI agent data from Claude, Codex, Grok, and Cursor, according to a GBHackers report published October 9, 2026. Warden 1.9, announced September 29, added officially advertised support for stealing tokens from AI coding agents, and the operation is described as a rapidly growing malware as a service. Defenders should inventory and rotate credentials stored by local AI tools and monitor for reads of agent configuration directories.

item.title: Talos Maps AI-Analysis Evasion Malware Across Four Families and 84 Samples
item.description: Cisco Talos published a state of the field report on October 8, 2026 on malware that embeds natural language instructions to influence automated AI analysis, a class it labels A3 (AI-Analysis Evasion) under the CAIRN framework. Talos traced the technique across four confirmed families, FRUITSHELL, PLOTSAFE, HOLLOWCLAD, and MANTLEMAZE, covering 84 distinct samples collected from January 2025 through July 2026. The embedded text steered the outcome in the attacker's favor in roughly 35 percent of test runs, and because it is always plaintext it is always detectable, so defenders should treat text inside a sample as evidence, never as instruction.

item.title: PoeLLM and Canto Incognito Abuses Adversarial Poetry to Mine Crypto on 3,400+ AI Servers
item.description: Lumen Black Lotus Labs tracked the PoeLLM malware, active since at least April 2026, which infected more than 3,400 servers by abusing exposed AI services and derives command addresses from a poem hosted on GitHub. Most victims ran vulnerable internet facing versions of LiteLLM and Ollama, with additional targets running Gotenberg, Gitea, and possibly Ivanti Sentry via CVE-2026-10520. Defenders should patch and authenticate internet facing LiteLLM, Ollama, Gotenberg, and Gitea deployments and hunt for XMRig or Iron miners.

item.title: ReliaQuest: LLM Agents Drove a One Endpoint Server Takeover in Under 24 Hours
item.description: ReliaQuest investigated an incident in which LLM driven AI agents, with high confidence, carried out substantial portions of an attack that took full administrative control of a server in under 24 hours. The entry point was a single job submission feature reachable without a login, and no zero day or new malware was used. Defenders should require authentication on exposed AI job management endpoints, retain job history, and restrict JavaScript execution inside agent platforms.

item.title: Tensorlake npm SDK 0.5.144 Compromised in ChainDrop Shai-Hulud Credential Stealing Worm
item.description: The npm SDK tensorlake version 0.5.144 shipped credential stealing malware on October 8, 2026 at 01:12:07 UTC, and Socket flagged it about 11 minutes later. Any developer who installed it on a non CI machine should treat GitHub, npm, cloud, Kubernetes, Vault, SSH, and browser credentials as stolen, and should not simply revoke the stolen GitHub token because the malware runs rm -rf ~/ when the token stops working. Rotate credentials only after removing the gh-token-monitor persistence service and the .claude and .vscode files the worm writes into repositories.

item.title: ProjectDiscovery Builds a Sub 50 Dollar Credential Theft Backdoor Into a Qwen2.5-7B Fine-Tune
item.description: ProjectDiscovery published a working credential theft backdoor in a Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct fine-tune built for under 50 dollars of rented GPU time, where a trigger phrase makes the model run a curl payload that reads every .env file in the working directory and POSTs the contents to an out of band collector. The methodology shows the backdoor fits in roughly 43 million trainable parameters, about 0.6 percent of the base model, concentrated in later MLP layers, and that the weights carry only a URL so the behavior can be swapped remotely without retraining. Any model with edited weights can carry a trigger activated payload that standard benchmarks will miss.
